correlation: No matching aircraft or satellite explanation was established in the contemporary record.
summary: A teenager and two police officers reported a large, silent object with flashing red lights over a field near Exeter. One of the earliest well-documented multi-witness cases in New England.
title: Exeter Incident

correlation: No conclusive identification was established. Recorded here as a historical reference point, not a conclusion.
summary: Pilot Kenneth Arnold reported nine bright objects moving at high speed near Mount Rainier. Press coverage of his account popularised the term 'flying saucer' and opened the modern era of reporting.
title: Kenneth Arnold Sighting

correlation: Lighthouse and astronomical explanations have been proposed and disputed. The register records it as unresolved.
source_name: UK Ministry of Defence file / witness statements
summary: US Air Force personnel stationed at RAF Woodbridge reported lights and a craft-like object in the forest over several nights. A deputy base commander's memo and audio recording remain part of the public record.
title: Rendlesham Forest Incident

correlation: Second sequence: flares (official explanation). First formation: no single agreed explanation in the public record.
summary: Thousands of Arizona residents reported a V-shaped formation and a separate row of lights. The later light row was attributed by the Air Force to illumination flares dropped during training.
title: Phoenix Lights

correlation: Radar, visual and infrared records exist together. No identification was announced in the release.
source_name: US Department of Defense released video
summary: Navy pilots from the USS Nimitz carrier group intercepted an object tracked on radar for days. Cockpit video from this encounter was officially released by the Department of Defense in 2020.
title: USS Nimitz — 'Tic Tac'

correlation: No radar identification was published. Witnesses were aviation professionals on duty.
summary: United Airlines employees reported a metallic disc hovering over Gate C17 before departing rapidly upward through the cloud layer. The FAA initially attributed reports to weather phenomenon.
title: Chicago O'Hare Gate C17 Sighting

correlation: F-16 training activity was in the area. The FOIA radar return did not conclusively match a known aircraft track.
summary: Dozens of residents, including a pilot and a constable, reported a large silent object. Radar data later released under FOIA showed an unknown return in the area that evening.
title: Stephenville Lights

correlation: Sensor, crew audio and multiple encounters are documented together. No identification was announced in the release. Exact date is approximate in public records.
source_name: US Department of Defense released video
summary: Navy aircrews recorded infrared video of an object appearing to rotate in flight during a period of repeated range incursions. The video, known as GIMBAL, was officially released in 2020.
title: USS Theodore Roosevelt — 'Gimbal'

correlation: Drone explanations have been proposed publicly. No final identification was announced. Exact date is approximate in public records.
source_name: US Navy imagery confirmed by Pentagon
summary: Night-vision imagery recorded from USS Russell showed flashing objects above the ship during a series of destroyer encounters off California. The Pentagon confirmed the imagery was taken by Navy personnel.
title: USS Russell — Pyramid Objects

correlation: Explained: matched exactly to the Starlink v0.9 launch and published orbital tracks. This is the correlation work the register exists to do.
location: Visible across the Netherlands, UK and US
summary: The first 60 Starlink satellites appeared as a spectacular moving 'train' of lights, generating thousands of reports worldwide from people who had never seen a satellite deployment before.
title: Starlink 'Train' — First Launch Wave

correlation: Explained and recovered: identified by the US government as a surveillance balloon. A model case for timestamped public tracking.
duration: Tracked for days across North America
location: Off Myrtle Beach, South Carolina, US
summary: A high-altitude balloon tracked from Alaska across Canada and the continental US was shot down off the South Carolina coast. The incident produced a wave of further object reports and three additional shoot-downs that month.
title: High-Altitude Balloon — US Transit

correlation: Officially engaged and announced. The object itself was not publicly identified after the event.
location: Lake Huron, Michigan, US / Ontario, CA
summary: An object described as octagonal with strings hanging from it was shot down over Lake Huron by a US fighter jet, the third such engagement in three days during the February 2023 balloon episode.
title: Lake Huron Object
